extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing and submitting articles to arXiv (researchers, students, and affiliated authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and submitting scholarly articles to the arXiv repository, covering allowed file formats, figure handling, metadata, timing/announcement rules, and author responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered submitters only
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions only from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Everyone who submits should read the general information; submissions must be made via the Submit form or START NEW SUBMISSION from your user page.

rubrics_metrics.name: License requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must grant arXiv.org a non-exclusive and irrevocable license to distribute or certify that the work is available under another license that conveys these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required legal/rights condition for all submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed text formats (order of preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission must be in one of the following formats (listed in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX; PDF; PostScript; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv's goal is to store articles in portable, stable formats; TeX/LaTeX is preferred because it is an open format that preserves information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit dvi/PS/PDF generated from TeX as final
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are using TeX/LaTeX, provide source in the preferred way (LaTeX/AMSLaTeX/PDFLaTeX workflows).

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-processor users: save as PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: Users of word processors such as Microsoft Word (versions prior to Word 2007) should save their documents as PDF and submit that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the PDF is not a scanned document (scanned documents are not accepted).

rubrics_metrics.name: No scanned documents
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will not accept scanned documents, regardless of format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scanned PDFs or image-only representations of papers are unacceptable because they do not preserve underlying text information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted figure formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures can be in common formats including PostScript (PS/EPS) for line drawings/plots, JPEG (ideal for photographic images), GIF or PNG (best for non-photographic images/bitmaps), and PDF figures (only with PDFLaTeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the format appropriate to the figure type (line art vs photographic) to preserve quality and portability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure size and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If figure files are too large, readers with poor network connections may not be able to download them; reduce size where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv has many users with poor network connections (e.g., in some developing nations); keep figures reasonably sized. If you have problems with a large submission, contact arXiv administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not omit figures/tables/sections
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv does not accept submissions with omitted figures, tables or sections. We also do not accept 'abstract only' submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing links to figures hosted on other servers does not substitute for including them; such submissions will be rejected as unhelpful and of limited archival value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include figures in LaTeX source with standard macros
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit figures with your (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., the graphics and graphicx packages) so that the figures will appear in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv administration cannot provide TeX-related help; seek help from colleagues for TeX issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will accept only the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =. Presence of any other character (e.g., spaces, question marks, asterisks, etc.) will cause the system to reject the file upload or submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These restrictions ensure maximum portability of stored files and minimize archival risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name case sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are case sensitive on arXiv. The file names Figure1.PDF and figure1.pdf are not the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether your local system is case sensitive or not, ensure internal file references (e.g., LaTeX figure inclusion commands) match case exactly to avoid broken references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited facilities for ancillary files/data sets
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files (data, programs, etc.) associated with articles submitted to arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the separate instructions about including data sets and ancillary files for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract metadata rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Title/Abstract information must be prepared according to separate instructions; this metadata is used on abstract pages, in announcements, in RSS feeds, and to support searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the separate title/abstract preparation instructions to ensure correct display and discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check submission and processed files before final submit
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making the final 'Submit Article' step, check carefully both the title/abstract (metadata) and the processed files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you see errors or are unhappy with formatting, correct them before final submit or contact arXiv administrators if problems cannot be resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsubmit to correct before announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you discover an error after submission but before public announcement, select the Unsubmit icon next to the submission on your user page to return it to incomplete status allowing modification and later resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsubmitting removes the article from the processing queue; announcement will be scheduled based on the later resubmission time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing/replacing and versioning rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Edits before an article is publicly announced will not generate additional versions. The date stamp associated with the submission will be the time that the final 'Submit Article' step is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT make a new submission for a corrected article or erratum; replace the original submission. Edits and final submission before 16:00 US Eastern Mon–Fri will not delay announcement. Edits between 16:00 and 20:00 will remove the submission from that day's announcements and delay it until the next day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing and announcement order
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are normally announced on a daily schedule; submissions before 16:00 US Eastern Mon–Fri are made publicly available after 20:00 US Eastern the same day (with examples provided for other days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are assigned identifiers and appear in listings in order based on the submission time (the last time the 'Submit' button was selected). An edit and subsequent 'Submit' will reset this time and thus change position in the listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsibility and required metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must make their own submissions; institutional affiliation for the author(s) and official report number(s) from the author(s)' institution(s) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions (e.g., by secretaries) are discouraged as they often cause problems. See also special instructions for third party submission and index submissions for conference proceedings.
